problem: Re-examine previously used strategy families without pooling incompatible versions or assuming every loss is strategy failure.
decision: Preserve mechanisms with confirmed implementation defects or competitive same-clock evidence, but do not restore an unchanged route solely from a favorable live slice. Every restored route requires a distinct strategy identity, exact contract parity, and a prospective scorecard scoped to that version and symbol set.

cases.finding: The same hype_breakout_onset_bidirectional_v1 identity represented both the HYPE-only contract and later BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE transfers. It also crossed different sizing generations. Aggregating those results as one strategy scorecard is invalid even when the signal source code was unchanged.
cases.economic_evidence: The early HYPE-only live slice was favorable, but the generic historical control was negative and later live generations were mixed. Universal early locks and the tested 5-minute momentum exit reduced returns. The promising observation is therefore mechanism-specific, not evidence that every route carrying the reused ID should be restored.
cases.action: Keep the generic reused identity out of the successor. Retain the separately named HYPE compression breakout/pullback challenger and require any native-onset retest to receive a new HYPE-only identity and independent forward ledger.
cases.confidence: high on identity contamination; low-medium on recoverable HYPE edge
cases.falsifier: A source-bound reconstruction proves the reused identity had one invariant symbol, sizing, entry, and exit contract, or a new predeclared HYPE-only version remains non-positive after exact costs and largest-winner removal.

cases.finding: V1 used a 30-second freshness contract rather than the researched 15-second contract. V2 narrowed the number but still used receipt age, allowed one-snapshot evidence, and reconstructed prior onset state in a way delayed receipts could rewrite.
cases.economic_evidence: Five linked v1 live closes lost $2.713721, but those outcomes cannot qualify the corrected pressure mechanism because all five used stale decision pressure under the frozen research contract.
cases.action: Keep v1/v2 retired. Continue v3 exact exchange-boundary, multi-snapshot, persisted-onset prospective capture under distinct report-only identities before routing.
cases.falsifier: Exact raw ledgers prove the linked v1 decisions met the 15-second contract, or v3 decisions fail raw-book parity.

cases.finding: The shared ETH/SOL provider incorrectly applied ETH's 60-bps stop to SOL although the frozen SOL recommendation used 80 bps. Signal parity checks found no missing-trigger defect; its hourly-cross entry mechanism is genuinely sparse.
cases.economic_evidence: The 80-bps cross-era variant led the compared stop contracts, while five exact missing-hourly-cross counterfactuals lost 62.91 bps in aggregate. Relaxing the cross would therefore have worsened the observed sample.
cases.action: Retain SOL Range with the repaired 80-bps override. Do not loosen the hourly cross merely to increase frequency; audit every future completed cross against the ledger.
cases.confidence: high on defect and liveness; low-medium on expectancy
cases.falsifier: A valid completed cross is absent from the provider ledger, or independent 60-bps outcomes outperform 80 bps after identical costs and path evidence.

cases.finding: The implementation produced a real, tradable signal family rather than random entries. Its 12-hour exit was the least contradicted tested duration, but neither side nor alignment subgroup was stable in both development and opened-final partitions.
cases.economic_evidence: In the shared-capital, same-clock comparison, ETH dual-MTF Range exceeded pullback net PnL under nominal and stress friction in development, opened-final, and full opened descriptive windows. The respective nominal deltas were +$1.1085, +$1.3556, and +$2.5886.
cases.action: Preserve pullback research and exact 12-hour contract, but keep ETH dual-MTF Range in the successor. Reopen pullback only through a new causal mechanism rather than another post-hoc side split.
cases.falsifier: A predeclared pullback revision beats dual-MTF Range on the same timestamps, capital, costs, chronological partitions, and largest-winner sensitivity.

cases.finding: The exact deployed-shape replay produced signals and exits normally; the observed weakness is not explained by a dead provider or absent order path.
cases.economic_evidence: The one-year deployed-shape replay completed 782 trades, lost $17.8237 on $500, produced PF 0.6193, and paid $13.0824 in modeled fees. Alternative stop/target geometry tested during re-examination remained negative across chronological partitions.
cases.action: Do not restore the unchanged Source Follow contract. Any successor must introduce a new causal entry mechanism, not only a payoff-grid change.
cases.confidence: high on deployed-shape failure; medium on broader family conclusion
cases.falsifier: A source-identical replay with corrected venue evidence materially changes these results, or a new predeclared entry mechanism is positive across untouched partitions after exact friction.

cases.finding: The literal 9/21 EMA plus Heikin-Ashi color and buy/sell alignment was tested, as were separately tuned 50/200 variants. Both were validation-negative across the evaluated HIP-3 assets; isolated live winners were largest-winner dependent.
cases.economic_evidence: The existing validation reports are negative for SP500, SPCX, SNDK, GOLD, and BRENTOIL under both the literal control and tuned candidate families.
cases.action: Keep the unchanged Swing/HA identity retired. A future version must add a genuinely new causal mechanism and receive a new identity.
cases.falsifier: An exact translation discrepancy is demonstrated, or a new mechanism survives independent validation and largest-winner removal.

continue_report_only: a future distinctly named HYPE-only onset challenger
portfolio_implications.live_transition: No running position, order, backend, profile, or execution authority is changed by this review. The repaired successor remains subject to flat-and-order-free transition validation.

limitations: Historical replays, live closes, and prospective observer rows use different windows and cannot be pooled into one expectancy estimate.
Correcting software or identity defects does not prove profitability.
A favorable live slice with few trades remains vulnerable to regime luck and largest-winner concentration.
The running v39 backend remains authoritative until a separately approved flat and order-free transition.
